data.why: CurveCurator ships bundled example datasets with matching TOML configs; the viability_CTRP_40 dataset (dose_responses_40.0.tsv, 1246 cell-line dose-response series) is small, uses the simple generic Name+Raw-column format, and its parameters_40.0.toml is re-run during install to regenerate a fresh curves_40.0.txt and dashboard_40.0.html from the current code.

goals: fit 4-parameter dose-response curves to viability data and inspect which cell lines show a genuine sigmoidal response versus noise
use the volcano plot (log2 fold change vs. significance/relevance score) to separate significant hits from the bulk of unaffected samples
switch to the potency plot to compare pEC50 potency estimates across the significant curves only
select individual curves by clicking or lasso-selecting in the volcano plot and read off their raw dose-response points and fitted curve in the curve panel and data table
use the pEC50/score/signal sliders and the regex-capable name search box to filter down to a specific subset of curves of interest
interpret unclassified (not up/down/not) curves correctly using the regulation categories and relevance score shown in the table

review.summary: The tree states clearly what the CurveCurator dashboard is for: separating relevant curves from noise with the 2D threshold, then looking at, comparing and narrowing the fitted curves. Its phases, tasks and features are well cut and nearly all are backed by the screens. Before filing it needs small fixes: the Save task cites a screen that shows no save, the 'Reset clears selection' claim is unverified, and deselection (ESC, Ctrl-click) from the README is missing.
